scope.description: A node left with an empty configuration by a RestoreCommittedLogs restart is asked for a vote by an outside candidate, then restored to contact with its leader while the leader appends one ordinary configuration entry, and asked for the same vote again.
assumptions: Each probe is preceded by a one-second isolation (twenty heartbeat timeouts) so that the node knows no leader and any election gate has had its chance to fire; the answer therefore reflects the configuration the node holds.
Both probes carry a term one above the target's current term and a last log entry equal to the target's, so the term branch and the log up-to-dateness branch cannot produce a refusal.

The configuration entry is produced by the cluster's own AddVoter API on the node that is leader at that moment, so the entry is an ordinary committed configuration change rather than a hand-written log record.
The node's snapshot store stays empty (ten-minute interval), so any change to its configuration must come from the AppendEntries configuration path.
The outsider identity P is connected to the node under test only and is never part of any configuration.
excluded: No snapshot install is used, so the installSnapshot repair path is not exercised here.
The new member D has no stores or transport, so it never votes and the change commits without it.
No snapshot failure or crash is injected.

basis.prefix: The harness builds three in-memory transports in a full mesh with per-node in-memory commit-tracking stores and snapshot stores, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, starts the three nodes with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and MockFSM, elects B as leader, applies ten commands, takes no snapshot on A and emits a 'fixture' event with A's snapshot count, staged commit index, last log index, live configuration and the configuration recorded in its log. It disconnects A from B and C, samples for one second and sends a RequestVote to A on behalf of the probe identity P - which appears in no configuration of the cluster - with a term one above A's and a last log entry equal to A's, emitting 'configured_probe' with the configured server count, the configuration ids, whether the candidate is in that configuration, whether a leader is known, whether campaigning was observed, the probe term, the response term, whether the vote was granted and the state. It shuts A down, replaces its transport, reconnects it, restarts it from the same stores with the feature enabled and emits 'restart_with_feature' with the returned flag, state, last applied index, reported configuration and the configuration recorded in A's log. It disconnects A again, samples for one second, repeats the identical probe and emits 'empty_config_probe' with the same operands. It then reconnects A, calls AddVoter for a new member D on the node that is leader, waits 600ms and emits 'after_configuration_entry' with A's configured server count, A's configuration ids, whether A holds the new member, the error from the configuration change future, A's last log index, A's staged commit index, the leader's own configuration ids, the leader's state, A's leader address and A's state. Finally it disconnects A again, samples for one second, repeats the identical probe and emits 'repaired_probe' with the same operands as the earlier probes. Event order: fixture, configured_probe, restart_with_feature, empty_config_probe, after_configuration_entry, repaired_probe.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft configuration recovery: r.configurations is refilled only by the AppendEntries configuration entry path or an installSnapshot, and vote admission admits any candidate while that configuration is empty.

comparisons.description: Control: while the node holds the committed configuration and knows no leader, the outside candidate is refused.
After the feature-enabled restart the configuration is empty and the identical probe is granted.
One ordinary configuration entry replicated to the node refills its configuration with the new membership.
With the configuration refilled, the same outside candidate is refused again.
The refusal is attributable to membership: the candidate is outside the refilled configuration and the node knows no leader.
